name: What is the difference between partial pool removal and full pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What exactly gets removed in a partial pool demolition versus a full pool removal?
mainEntity.text: What exactly gets removed in a partial pool demolition versus a full pool removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial removal is the lower-cost option and is often used when the homeowner wants to reclaim the yard without paying for complete excavation. In a partial removal, contractors remove the upper shell, create drainage openings, and fill the remaining space with clean soil and compact it. In a full removal, the entire shell, including the bottom and walls, is excavated and hauled away before the area is backfilled and compacted. Full removal is usually preferred when the property may be regraded, landscaped heavily, or built on later. It also reduces the chance of future sinking or unexpected remnants below grade. Partial removal is faster and cheaper, but it can leave buried structural material behind. A good estimate should clearly state which method is being used, what debris is hauled off, and how compaction is handled. That distinction affects cost, timeline, and future use of the yard.
acceptedAnswer.description: Partial pool removal typically means breaking down the top portion of the shell, punching drainage holes, and backfilling the cavity. Full pool removal means excavating and hauling away the entire shell, then backfilling and compacting the site. Full removal costs more but leaves less long-term settlement risk.
